answer: When agents trade reef feeds, forecast zephyr winds, or analyze nebula data, a network can curb Sybil nodes via TPM Direct Anonymous Attestation. Each agent binds its signing key to a Trusted Platform Module and submits a zero-knowledge proof scoped to an epoch basename, letting peers detect duplicate tags from one chip without learning its serial number. Attackers must therefore buy distinct hardware per identity, though rogue vendors or side-channel key extraction can bypass this limit.
